props.title: The evolving interface between humans and agents.
props.lead: Your agent's answers become interfaces — interactive, archived, and evolving as you use them.

content.text: ShowAI works inside the agent you already use: the plugin lets your agent build interfaces, and the ShowAI app keeps, opens and edits them.
This guide goes from download to your first interface, then shows how to keep working on it and share it.
Before you start
You need a Mac with Apple silicon (macOS 13 or later), and Claude Code or Codex signed in. No agent yet? Use the built-in agent with a model API key.
Your agent's command-line tool must work.
ShowAI installs its plugin through the agent's own plugin commands. In a terminal,
claude --version
or
codex --version
should print a version number; Codex can also use the command-line tool bundled with the Codex app, which ShowAI finds automatically.
No agent yet?
Add a model API key in the app and use the built-in agent; see “Without Claude Code or Codex” on this page.
On Windows or Linux?
Run the browser edition from source; see
Installation & Setup
1. Install ShowAI

steps.title: Download DMG
steps.body: Download the DMG from the [latest release](https://github.com/Renaissance-Mind/ShowAI/releases/latest) on GitHub.

steps.title: Drag to Applications, then open it
steps.body: Open the DMG, drag **ShowAI** into Applications, then open ShowAI from Applications.
steps.result: On first launch, ShowAI shows the welcome screen.

content.text: Blocked by macOS on first launch?
Current builds are not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS may block the first launch. If it does, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway (see
Apple's instructions
). Each release's notes say whether this is still needed.
2. Connect your agent

steps.title: Open the plugin panel
steps.body: The welcome screen shows the plugin panel on first launch; after that, find it under Settings → Plugins at any time.

steps.title: Install plugin
steps.body: ShowAI checks for Claude Code and Codex. Click Install plugin next to the agent you use.

steps.title: Reload the agent
steps.body: Restart the Claude Code session, or refresh plugins or restart Codex.

steps.title: Start a new conversation
steps.body: A conversation that was already open keeps its old tool list, so continue in a new one.

content.text: To confirm the connection, Settings → Plugins shows a test prompt, “Use ShowAI to list my projects”. Send it in a new conversation; when the agent reaches ShowAI, the status next to that agent changes from “Waiting for the first call” to “First call received”.

The app supplies both the plugin and the runtime it talks to, so you need neither the source code nor a separate Node.js installation. The plugin connects to the app's current content library; click Update and enable after switching libraries or moving the app.
If the panel says the agent wasn't found, shows “Installed, disabled”, or reports a plugin from another source, see
Connecting an agent: common problems
3. Ask for your first interface
Paste this into a new conversation:
Use ShowAI to build a mortgage calculator: price, down payment, rate and term are adjustable; show the monthly payment and total interest.
The agent saves the interface as a page in ShowAI and presents it: inline in agents that can display it, otherwise as an HTML file you can open. In the app it appears under Recent.
Two more to try:
Use ShowAI to compare two foldable phones on portability, battery, camera and price, and let me adjust the weights.
Use ShowAI to explain attention step by step, with a diagram whose parameters I can adjust to see the weights change.
Does the agent answer only in text, or say it can't find ShowAI? The conversation may have started before the plugin loaded; see
Connecting an agent: common problems
4. Keep working on it
The interface is a page you own. Open it from Recent and edit it directly: type text, or type
to insert tables, charts, images and other components. When the save status shows “Saved on this device”, your changes are stored.
Then ask the agent to continue:
Add a chart of the remaining balance by year. Keep the values I changed.
The agent reads the current page, including your edits, before it changes anything. Click Next to step through what happens in one creation and one follow-up edit.

steps.label: Paste the mortgage calculator prompt
steps.detail: Say what you want. To put it in a particular project, name the project in the prompt.

steps.label: Build and save the interface
steps.detail: The agent builds the interface from components such as sliders and charts and first saves it as a page in a project. If no project is named, the project is chosen from the agent's current working directory.

steps.label: Return a page ready to present
steps.detail: Agents that can display it inline show it in the conversation; other agents give you an HTML file to open.

steps.label: Page appears in Recent
steps.detail: The plugin and the app use the same content library, so you can open the page in the app right away.

steps.label: Change a few values
steps.detail: Your edits save automatically, and the status shows “Saved on this device”.

steps.label: “Add a remaining-balance chart”
steps.detail: Ask the agent to build on your edits.

steps.label: Read the current page, then save
steps.detail: The agent reads the latest version, including your edits, and saves with the version number it read.

steps.label: Save paused if the page changed meanwhile
steps.detail: If you and the agent change the same page at the same time, the later save is paused and both versions are kept for comparison, so **neither overwrites the other**.

content.text: When an interface needs something the existing components can't express, the agent can build a new component for it. A page that works well can become a template for the next one. See
Components & Templates
5. Share it
Format
Use
Standalone HTML
Send a single page, read it offline or archive it
Inline fragment
Preview the whole page or a selection in an agent conversation that can display HTML
static website
Publish several pages as a site with navigation
ShowAI JSON
Import and continue editing
Choose Export page in the page's menu, or ask the agent. Standalone HTML opens in any browser without ShowAI and keeps interactions such as charts, collapsible sections and local calculations.
External links still need a network; for fully offline reading, embed images in the page. HTML exports also write a
.showai.json
source so the page can be imported and edited later. For how the formats differ, see
Export & Share
Without Claude Code or Codex

cards.title: Built-in Agent
cards.body: Open Settings → Agent and add a model source with an API key (or use your local Codex or Claude Code sign-in, or ShowAI Cloud). Then click the AI button in the top bar, or select text or open a block menu and choose Ask AI.

cards.title: Other agents
cards.body: DeepSeek Harness and Kimi are in preview, ChatGPT on the web is invite only, and Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other MCP clients can be configured manually.

cards.title: Use the workbench on its own
cards.body: The workbench works without an agent: click New project, add a Page for content in reading order or a Board for placing content freely, and type `/` to insert components.
